suggestions.assertion: Uses gh pr create (not gh api or other approach)
suggestions.reason: This assertion would pass even if the command were syntactically incorrect or missing critical flags — it only checks that 'gh pr create' appears somewhere. The other assertions cover specific flags, so this is mostly redundant as a quality gate, but it does serve as a useful sanity check for the approach.

No assertion checks whether the command is actually syntactically valid and runnable. The response produced a well-formed command, but a garbled command that happened to contain all the right flag names would also pass all 7 assertions. Consider adding an assertion like 'The gh pr create command is syntactically correct and could be copy-pasted to run'.

No assertion checks the quality of the PR body beyond the auto-close keyword. The response included a structured Summary and Test Plan, which adds real value. An assertion like 'Body includes a meaningful summary of the changes' would reward higher-quality outputs.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions are well-targeted and cover all the explicit requirements from the prompt. They form a strong set for verifying flag-level correctness. The main gap is that they don't test the overall quality or runnability of the output beyond checking individual flags.
